gaps.sentence: After the long journey, we were all ___ (EXHAUST).
gaps.explanation: People who experience the feeling take -ed: we were exhausted. The journey was exhausting.

gaps.sentence: The sky began to ___ as the storm approached (DARK).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: darken means to become dark. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: It was the most ___ (FORGET) trip of my life.
gaps.hint: negative adjective: too good to forget
gaps.explanation: 'Unforgettable' = impossible to forget; 'forgetful' describes a person who forgets.

gaps.sentence: The government wants to ___ the tax system (SIMPLE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: simplify means to make simple. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (CONFIDENT) was shaken by the failure.
She was fired for ___ behaviour at work (PROFESSIONAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'behaviour'
gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unprofessional behaviour is behaviour below professional standards.

gaps.sentence: The delay was caused by a simple ___ (UNDERSTAND).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed: they understood wrongly (mis-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: a misunderstanding is a failure to understand correctly.

gaps.sentence: The mixture will ___ as it cools (SOLID).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: solidify means to become solid. A base verb follows 'will'.
